prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glues

statement.case_for: After reading the full first round I keep my configuration: B056 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The principle is the kind I look for in a prize, a simple chemical idea (a small molecule that brings a ligase and a target into one ternary complex) with event-driven, catalytic pharmacology that is quantitatively understood and has been reproduced by many independent groups. Seven of eight members put B056 in their preferred configuration, and the scientific description is the same in every file. What remains is the third seat, and I weigh it by asking which names rest on a distinct, datable discovery. Crews and Deshaies carry the PROTAC concept and first proof of principle. Handa's identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide is a separate mechanistic discovery that explains an old drug, defines the molecular-glue strand, and underlies most CRBN-recruiting degraders. Ciulli's VHL ligands and cooperativity work are important and I value the quantitative biophysics, but as a simulation person I read them as the rigorous refinement of a mechanism that already existed, not as a founding step. A citation on recruiting ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins covers both strands without naming everyone, and it rests on chemistry and mechanism, not on approvals.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that a single citation may blur two lineages, PROTACs and cereblon glues, and that Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim all have real claims that three seats cannot honour. If the expert reports show that the VHL ligand and ternary-complex framework is substantially independent of the Crews laboratory, the case for Ciulli over Handa becomes stronger than I now judge it. The clinical case is also still partly prospective, since no degrader is yet a broadly approved therapy, although I accept Sparr's argument that waiting for a regulatory event would make the prize hostage to it.

responses.point: Linke prefers Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli because PROTAC design is a transferable principle and Ciulli's structural basis and cooperativity work made degraders drug-like and quantitative, while Handa's work is the discovery of a target of an existing drug class; he says he can be persuaded that cereblon was the more decisive step.
responses.response: This is the cleanest statement of the alternative and I take it seriously. My difference is in what counts as the discovery. Cooperativity and VHL ligand design generalised and optimised a concept that Crews and Deshaies had already shown, whereas cereblon is the only part of the story that explained how a drug in clinical use acts and opened a second mechanism, the glue, that was not designed at all. I also note that your own citation wording would cover the glue strand while the names would not, which is the awkward outcome I would like to avoid. I therefore keep Handa, but I would accept your wording about induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases for the citation.

responses.point: Zou says Handa's work explains a drug class that was already clinical, that if Handa is chosen the citation must say whether it covers both strands, and that Ciulli's structural basis for VHL ligands would be the name displaced; she says she would accept Handa if the committee chooses him.
responses.response: I agree that the citation must state the scope, and mine does: it names the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues explicitly. I accept that Ciulli is the name displaced and that this is a real cost. I weigh the structure-based work on VHL as strong support for the design principle, but the structural evidence for the ternary complex has come from several groups, whereas cereblon as the thalidomide target is one identification with a clear date and clear authors. Your willingness to accept Handa matters, since it brings the configuration within reach of a majority.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers Crews, Deshaies and Handa because each name rests on a distinct datable discovery, regards Ciulli's work as a strong line of work and not a single attributable discovery, and asks the expert report to show how much of the ternary-complex framework is attributable to Ciulli rather than shared with Crews.
responses.response: I agree with the criterion and with the request to the expert report, and I would make it a condition: if the report shows that the VHL ligand and cooperativity framework is a distinct, first-in-kind contribution outside the Crews group, I would reopen the third seat. His own point that naming Handa could be read as awarding two discoveries in one citation is the fair counterweight, and I answer it by wording the citation around one principle, recruiting a ligase to remove a chosen protein, with PROTACs and cereblon glues as its two demonstrations.

responses.point: Somfai still prefers Pd-catalysed C-N coupling with Buchwald and Hartwig, a mature method with clean two-person credit, and doubts how much is chemically new in degraders, describing much of it as ligand and linker optimisation around existing biology.
responses.response: The credit for C-N coupling is indeed cleaner and the adoption is easy to verify, and I take that seriously as a maturity argument. But on novelty I disagree: recruiting a ligase to a target is a new mode of drug action and the cereblon mechanism is a discovery, not an optimisation, and the 2010 prize makes C-N coupling a harder case than you allow, since Sparr, Zou, Linke and I all see it as an extension of an honoured idea. I would keep it as a candidate for a later year and do not list it as an alternative. I note you list B056 as your first alternative, so your preferred configuration and the majority one do not conflict on the science.

responses.point: Chabes supports Crews, Deshaies and Handa because the cereblon discovery explained how an already-used drug acts and opened the molecular-glue branch, but he is recalling trial status and not verifying it, and would not split B056 unless no unified citation can be agreed.
responses.response: I agree, and I share the caution about recalled clinical status; that is a reason to build the citation on the mechanism and not on trial results. I also agree that splitting B056 into two parts is a worse outcome than a single citation that covers both strands, since two parts would exhaust the three-name limit on a single field and leave no room for the credit to stay clean. I would split only if no unified wording can be agreed.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports show that Ciulli's VHL ligand and ternary-complex work is a distinct, first-in-kind contribution, in which case the third seat should be reconsidered.

Whether a single citation can cover PROTACs and cereblon glues without being read as a compromise, and whether Sakamoto's co-authorship of the 2001 paper or Ito's role with Handa should change any seat.
Whether the lack of an approved degrader makes recognition early; I rely on recollection of trial status.
If B056 fails to reach five votes for one trio, whether B048 should be credited to Liu alone, given Nishida and Kondo's parallel work and the proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on B056 or on my alternatives B048 and B017. My Warshel and EVB connections and my computational biochemistry work are not tied to any shortlisted candidate. I have served on the committee with Peter Brzezinski since 2015, which is a committee relationship and not a conflict. Nothing in the first-round files changes this.
